summary: Montana-Idaho border peak; steel Aermotor lookout from 1938, dismantled 1974-76; a climbers' guide says only foundation blocks remain near the summit.

facts.design: Steel Aermotor tower erected 1938, with a log cabin
facts.status_note: Tower dismantled in 1974 per Forest Lookouts Montana; firelookout.com gives gone by 1976. Foundation blocks remain near the summit per SummitPost.
facts.agency: Lolo and St. Joe National Forests

staffing.status: lookouts named in newspaper notices, 1915 to 1947

access.note: A climbers' guide describes a hike from Freezeout Pass; no agency access rules were read

visit.trail_note: Relatively easy class 1 trail from Freezeout Pass, roughly 5 miles round trip, per a climbers' guide

corrections.why: firelookout.com gives the 1938 tower as 60 feet, and a 1943 newspaper item quoted on the Montana page also says 60-foot. None of the sources read gives 3.7 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com and a 1943 newspaper item say 60 feet; the Montana page quotes a 1938 item that says about 72 feet. The record uses 60 feet and the story gives both.
firelookout.com dates a log cabin and pole platform to 1913; a July 1915 newspaper item quoted on the Montana page describes a lookout station being set up. The story reports both dates.
The Montana page says the tower was dismantled in 1974; firelookout.com says gone by 1976. The story gives both.
firelookout.com says Lolo/St. Joe National Forests; the Montana page says Lolo National Forest; SummitPost places the peak on the border of both forests. The record uses both forests.

notes_for_editor: Brief height 3.7 m matches no source; corrected to 60 ft. Build date (1913 vs 1915) and tower end date (1974 vs 1976) conflict between firelookout.com and the Montana page. The summit-remains and trail details come from a climbers' guide (SummitPost), not an agency record, so no agency source was found for the site today. Access level 'public' rests on that guide alone.
